name: Broccoli
label: broccoli bed

planting.note: two rows of four, 18–24 in apart; one row of four is enough for a small household

bed30.note: two rows about 10 in apart across the 30 in bed; Johnny's spans 10–18 in between plants

watch_for: imported cabbageworm (green larvae in the head), cabbage root maggot — UMaine's most destructive brassica pest: wilting plants mean check the roots; flea beetles on seedlings; clubroot where brassicas have grown lately
watering: Even moisture; a dry spell at head formation makes small, loose heads.
method_notes: The fall crop is the Maine crop: UMaine plants broccoli from late June through early August for September–October harvest, and Fedco warns spring broccoli has gotten harder as summers warm — heat makes loose heads. Cut the center head before the buds open yellow; side shoots keep coming for weeks (UNH). Coleman's transplant-first discipline applies; direct seeding buys nothing in a short season (Cornell IPM guide).
source: UMaine Coop. Ext. planting chart (rows 24–36 in, in-row 24–30 in, plant 5/1–8/1) and 'Keep Your Garden Growing' (start 5–7 wks inside; early-August set-outs for fall); Cornell 2016 Organic Cole Crop IPM Guide (transplant, not direct-seed; 12–18 in in-row); UNH 'Growing Cole Crops'; Johnny's broccoli culture (DTM from transplant, +20 d direct; 10–18 in apart); Fedco broccoli (62–95 d from transplant; 'easier as a fall crop'); UMaine cabbage maggot & clubroot fact sheets; interplanting effect per Tahvanainen & Root 1972; Coleman, The New Organic Grower (3rd ed.), 'The Optimum Garden' (30-in beds, 12-in paths).

name: Cauliflower
label: cauliflower bed

planting.note: two rows of four, 18–24 in apart — one of the hungriest brassicas for space

bed30.note: two rows 10 in apart, 18 in between heads — it needs that room to make a good curd (Cornell: 15–24 in)

watch_for: buttoning — small useless heads from cold or drought stress on young plants (Cornell: a 10-day stretch of 40°F highs); cabbage root maggot; imported cabbageworm; aphids working into the curd
watering: Never let it dry out; drought or cold stress while young is exactly what causes buttoning.
method_notes: The most finicky of the cole crops (Cornell): mature heads are not resistant to hard freezes, so in Maine it is a fall crop — UMaine's late-June through early-August plantings. Pick self-blanching varieties and skip the tying; purple and orange types never need blanching (Cornell). Give it the richest, most evenly watered spot in the brassica block and it repays you; skip it if the bed is short.
source: Cornell Cauliflower growing guide (most finicky; heads not resistant to hard freezes; sow 4–6 wks inside; 15–24 in apart; buttoning from cold, variety choice for extended harvest); Cornell 2016 Organic Cole Crop IPM Guide (15–18 in in-row); UNH 'Growing Cole Crops'; UMaine Coop. Ext. 'Keep Your Garden Growing' (5–8 wks inside; early-August fall setting); Fedco veggie chart (transplants May, 24–30 in); Johnny's/Fedco catalog DTM ranges (early ~50 to late 75–80 d from transplant).

name: Cabbage
label: cabbage bed

planting.note: two rows of four; early compact heads can squeeze tighter, storage types want the whole 18 in

bed30.note: two rows 12 in apart; early varieties can try 3 rows at 12 in, storage types want 18 in (UMaine: 12–18 in in-row)

watch_for: cabbage root maggot, clubroot (UMaine: 4-yr rotation, keep pH at 6.8 or above), imported cabbageworm; mature heads split after heavy rain
watering: Steady water; a heavy soak after drought is what makes heads split.
method_notes: Grow two populations: early compact types for June–July, then storage types set by late June that ride out fall frosts — Fedco notes cabbage doubles its sugar after a month of cold, 'exposure to hoarfrost is good for cabbages.' Headed plants stand to ~20°F (UKy; young plants to 10–15°F for a night or two per UNH), which is what makes the storage class a November crop in open Maine beds.
source: Johnny's cabbage growing info (early spring DTM from transplant, +14 d direct; 12–18 in apart, rows 18–36 in); Fedco cabbage culture (DTM from transplant; frost sweetening; early to storage types ~60–110 d); UMaine Coop. Ext. planting chart (12–18 in in-row, plant 5/1–8/1) and 'Keep Your Garden Growing'; UNH 'Growing Cole Crops' (12 in, cold tolerance); UKy NEP-249 (headed cabbage to 20°F); UMaine cabbage maggot & clubroot fact sheets; Cornell 2016 Organic Cole Crop IPM Guide (transplant-first; 10–14 in fresh market, 18–24 in kraut).

name: Brussels sprouts
label: brussels sprouts bed

planting.note: two rows of three, 24 in apart — the longest-season brassica and it grows 2–3 ft tall

bed30.note: two rows 10–12 in apart; 18–24 in between plants (Johnny's), row cover until June against flea beetle and swede midge (Fedco)

watch_for: cabbage aphid — it tucks into the sprout and is hard to wash out; swede midge and flea beetles on young plants (row cover early — Fedco); cabbage root maggot's fall generation (UMaine)
watering: Deep, steady water all season; a dry spell makes loose, leafy sprouts.
method_notes: The patience crop: set out by mid-May (Fedco: start indoors no later than early April), then wait — flavor peaks after frost and sprouts harvest past the first snowfall (Fedco) or into December (Johnny's). Top the plants in early September when the lower sprouts are ½–¾ in for a uniform, once-over stalk (Johnny's, Fedco, UNH). Skip them if the brassica bed is short; Fedco wants ~9 sq ft a plant.
source: Johnny's brussels sprouts growing info (DTM from transplant, +20 d direct; 18–24 in apart, rows 30–36 in; top at ½–¾ in; harvest after frost to end of December); Fedco brussels culture (very cold hardy, harvest past first snowfall, top in early September, 9 sq ft/plant, 90–110 d from transplant); UNH 'Growing Cole Crops' (18 in, frost improves flavor, pinch tip early September); UMaine cabbage maggot fact sheet (fall generation attacks late crucifers); Cornell 2016 Organic Cole Crop IPM Guide (24 in in-row).

name: Kohlrabi
label: kohlrabi strip

planting.note: about 6 in apart in four short rows — it is small, fast, and crops twice

bed30.note: four rows 6–7 in apart; Fedco short-season spacing is 6–8 in, Johnny's fresh-market thinning is 4 in

watch_for: flea beetles (the main one — Fedco: row cover from day one), imported cabbageworm; bulbs turn woody and inedible if left too long
watering: Even moisture so the bulbs stay crisp; drought makes them woody.
method_notes: The fastest and most forgiving Cole crop: Johnny's grows it 'throughout the season in the North' and Fedco sows ASAP and again in August. Harvest at 2–3 in (Johnny's; storage types like Gigante to 8 in) — overgrown kohlrabi is the classic beginner disappointment. Coleman lists kohlrabi among his 30 cold-hardy winter vegetables (Winter Harvest Handbook), and Fedco's Kolibri wintered over under snow in Maine, so the late-August sowing carries into the cold months. Note: the edible bulb is a swollen stem, harvested like a root.
source: Johnny's kohlrabi growing info (DTM from direct seeding, ~14 d less from transplant; thin 4 in fresh-market, 10 in storage; harvest 2–3 in; cool-weather crop); Fedco veggie chart (sow ASAP & August; thin 6–8 in, rows 12–18 in; Gigante 12–18 in) and Kolibri page (45 d; wintered over under snow in Maine); Coleman, The Winter Harvest Handbook, cold-hardy vegetables chapter (kohlrabi on the 30-crop winter list).

name: Rapini (broccoli raab)
label: rapini rows

planting.note: three 8 ft rows, sown thick and thinned to 4–6 in — a cut-and-come-again green

bed30.note: three rows 8 in apart, thinned to 4–6 in (Gulley: 6–12 in); sow thick and cut young

watch_for: flea beetles on the young leaves, cabbage aphids in the buds; it bolts the moment it warms — buds open fast once weather turns hot
watering: Keep it cool and watered; bolting is the failure mode, not pests.
method_notes: Fast, cool-loving, and nearly pest-free in fall: direct-sow in April for spring or late summer for the fall flush, and harvest the budding shoots before the flowers open — expect a second and third flush over 2–4 weeks (Gulley). Coleman grows broccoli raab as a winter-harvest crop under cover (Winter Harvest Handbook's cold-hardy list); in open Wiscasset beds treat it as the earliest spring green and a September replant with a 2-week succession (Gulley). Early-spring direct sowings are the slow ones — up to 60 days — later sowings about 40 (IFAS).
source: Gulley Greenhouse rapini culture (45 d; sow 4–6 wks before last frost and again 8–10 wks before first frost; successive sowings 1–2 wks apart; thin to 6–12 in; harvest shoots 1–2 in across before flowers open); IFAS EDIS broccoli raab (spring seedings 60 d early, ~40 d later); Fedco Quarantina broccoli raab (DTM from transplant; brassica culture, direct seed May/June for fall); Coleman, The Winter Harvest Handbook, cold-hardy vegetables chapter (broccoli raab on the 30-crop winter list); Tahvanainen & Root 1972 for diversified-planting flea-beetle effect.

name: Napa cabbage
label: napa rows

planting.note: two rows of four, 15–18 in apart — big upright heads; direct-seed the fall crop instead

bed30.note: two rows 12 in apart; Johnny's direct-seeds 12–18 in apart in rows 18–30 in

watch_for: bolting — young plants exposed to frost or a week of nights under 50°F run to seed (Johnny's); flea beetles and slugs on seedlings; downy mildew and black rot on the fall crop in a wet season
watering: Even moisture from day one; stress while young is what triggers bolting.
method_notes: A fall crop in Maine: direct-sow late July so it heads in cool weather (Johnny's direct-seed window is late May to mid-July; DTM is from transplant, add 14–21 days from seed). Spring attempts are the risky ones — frost or a week of sub-50°F nights on young plants sends them to seed (Johnny's). It stands light frost (Fedco rates Chinese cabbage 'moderate'), so the fall harvest runs into November, and heads hold 1–2 months near freezing (Johnny's).
source: Johnny's Chinese cabbage growing info (DTM from transplant, +14–21 d direct; direct seed late May–mid-July, thin to 12–18 in, rows 18–30 in; bolting triggers; stores 1–2 months near freezing); Fedco veggie chart (Chinese cabbage: sow May, transplants 3–4 wks, thin 12–18 in, frost tolerance 'moderate'); UKy NEP-249 (Bilko 54 DTH); UMaine Coop. Ext. brassica pest fact sheets (cabbage maggot, clubroot); Cornell 2016 Organic Cole Crop IPM Guide (black rot, downy mildew in wet seasons).
